Welcome from the Head of School
Welcome to Barham Primary School — a caring, inclusive school at the heart of its community, where every child matters. Barham is a warm and purposeful place built on kindness, trust and high expectations. Families quickly feel the strong sense of belonging that defines our school, and children are known, valued and supported to flourish.Having served as a senior leader at Barham for over ten years, I feel deeply connected to our community and the journey we have shared. During this time, I have worked alongside staff and families to strengthen teaching, nurture talent and continually raise aspirations for our children. It is a privilege to now serve as Interim Head of School and to continue building on the strong foundations that define Barham — with clarity, care and confidence in our shared direction.At the heart of our work is a belief in learning that makes a lasting difference. We want children to enjoy coming to school, to feel curious and confident as learners, and to leave each day proud of their achievements and inspired by what lies ahead. Learning at Barham builds secure foundations, deepens understanding over time and nurtures the resilience, confidence and character children need to thrive — both now and in the future.

pageCache.pageTitle: Barham Primary School - Our Vision and Values
pageCache.text:
Our School Vision and Values
What we want for our children
We want all of our children to leave us equipped for life in the 21 Century- able to operate successfully in the changing world of work and take advantage of all opportunities available to them. Through understanding our global community and appreciating our children’s needs, we integrate specific learning experiences into our curriculum so that every child can achieve well at Bahram, transition well into their next phase of education and lead happy and fulfilled lives.
Our vision
Our curriculum starts with our vision of which our children are at the forefront.
We are safe, happy and kind learners
We are change makers
Our values
Integral to our coherent vision are five core values: respect, resilience, risk taking, reflectiveness, and resourcefulness, which provide a strategic framework for our development of the whole child. Through this character building, our children develop the necessary learning disciplines, aptitudes and attitudes to become the 21st century learner.

pageCache.text:
SMSC/British Values
Promoting British Values at Barham Primary School
The DfE have recently reinforced the need “to create and enforce a clear and rigorous expectation on all schools to promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs.” The Government set out its definition of British values in the 2011 Prevent Strategy, this advice and guidance was updated in June 2015 and the values reiterated. At Barham these values are reinforced regularly and in the following ways:
Democracy
Each year the children decide upon their class charter and the rights associated with these. All the children contribute to the drawing up of the charter.We have a student council which meets once per term with the Headteacher to discuss issues raised in class council meetings. The council has its own budget and is genuinely able to effect change within the school. Every child on the student council is voted in by their class. Children have an annual questionnaire where they are able to put forward their views about the school.
The Rule of Law
The importance of laws, whether they be those that govern the class, the school, or the country, are consistently reinforced at Barham. Pupils are taught from an early age the 5R’s and the Code of Conduct which are the rules of the school. These are our Golden Rules, Playground Rules and eSafety Rules. Pupils are taught the value and reasons behind rules and laws, that they govern and protect us, the responsibilities that this involves and the consequences when laws are broken. Visits to and from authorities such as the Police and Fire Service help reinforce this message.
Individual Liberty
At Barham, pupils are actively encouraged to make choices, knowing that they are in a safe and supportive environment. As a school we educate and provide boundaries for young pupils to make informed choices, through a safe environment and an empowering education. Pupils are encouraged to know, understand and exercise their rights and personal freedoms and advised how to exercise these safely, for example through our eSafety and PSHE lessons.
Mutual Respect
Mutual respect is at the heart of our mission and aims. Children learn that their behaviours have an effect on their own rights and those of others. All members of the school community treat each other with respect. The first of our Golden Rules reads: Be respectful. Our mission statement reads: Respecting each other.
Tolerance of those of Different Faiths and Beliefs
Barham is a diverse school. We actively promote diversity through our celebrations of different faiths and cultures. Religious Education lessons and PSHE lessons reinforce messages of tolerance and respect for others. Our multicultural pages on our website illustrate our commitment to exploring our diverse school community. Members of different faiths and religions are encouraged to share their knowledge to enhance learning within classes and the school. The children visit places of worship that are important to different faiths.
Spiritual, Moral, Social and Cultural (SMSC)
Barham Primary School has a strong commitment to the personal and social development of all pupils. The school vision and values, put together by all the staff, supports spiritual, moral, social and cultural characteristics in all pupils.
What is SMSC – Spiritual, Moral, Social and Cultural development?
Here is a summary to explain SMSC development – it is personalised for all our pupils at Barham.
Spiritual development is when we:
Explore beliefs and experience; respect faiths, feelings and values; enjoy learning about oneself, others and the surrounding world; use imagination and creativity; reflect.
Moral development is when we:
Recognise right and wrong; respect the law; understand consequences; investigate moral and ethical issues; offer reasoned views.
Social development is when we:
Use a range of social skills; participate in the local community; appreciate diverse viewpoints; participate, volunteer and cooperate; resolve conflict; engage with the 'British values' of democracy, the rule of law, liberty, respect and tolerance.
Cultural development is when we:
Appreciate cultural influences; appreciate the role of Britain's parliamentary system; participate in culture opportunities; understand, accept, respect and celebrate diversity.
In our school pupil’s SMSC development is seen for example in:
SMSC is embedded throughout the curriculum at Barham. This integrated approach ensures that aspects of SMSC is considered in all subject areas. The Strategic Leadership Team audits SMSC and Governors monitor it across school.
Developing an awareness and respect for diversity
Developing and appreciation of theatre
Developing an understanding of right and wrong.
Taking part in sporting opportunities.
Taking part in cultural opportunities.
Taking part in artistic opportunities.
Beyond the Curriculum
We are also committed as a school to developing SMSC beyond the curriculum. This is done through:
www.unicef.org.uk/rights-respecting-schools/
Impact
In order to reflect further on the impact of all our work on SMSC:
We engage governors, families and community
We listen to our pupils
Observe staff and pupil interactions
Support Social Behaviour

pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Executive Headteacher
Welcome to The Barham and Preston Park FederationWelcome to The Barham and Preston Park Federation — a bold new partnership between Barham and Preston Park, united through our shared purpose of delivering transformational learning. Our federation is an ambitious step forward, bringing two strong schools together so we can do even more for our children, families and dedicated staff team.Our schools are where spaces where children fall in love with learning. We want every child to feel inspired to learn, encouraged to think, and empowered to dream. We want our schools to be places where curiosity catches, confidence grows and pupils leave each day feeling proud of what they have achieved and excited about what comes next.Transformational learning is learning that develops the whole child. It is more than our inspiring curriculum and academic results. It means children build deep knowledge and real understanding, develop the confidence to apply what they know, and grow the character and skills to thrive. It is children leaving us ready for the next stage — believing, “I can do this,” and “I belong here,” as they step into their exciting futures.Federation gives us momentum and amplifies impact. It is not about us becoming the same. Rather it enables us to share the very best practice between our schools, learn from one another at pace, strengthen leadership capacity and create greater consistency, stability and opportunity for pupils. It also allows us to build a richer offer beyond the classroom, while keeping what makes each school special firmly at the centre of everything we do. Our work is grounded in collaboration, connection and care, so children feel safe, valued and proud, and thrive in a professional community built on trust, innovation and wellbeing.Our federation is driven by three values. Belonging is the promise that every child will be safe, known and included, and that our schools will feel like communities families can trust. Knowledge-Creation is our commitment to an ambitious curriculum and excellent teaching that build deep understanding, creativity and readiness for the modern world. Dynamic Leadership is how we deliver: values-led, trust-driven and grounded in integrity — calm, consistent leadership that keeps getting better.And above all, we are clear about what we are building together: Stronger Schools. Brighter Futures.Thank you for being part of this journey. We are proud of what our schools already are — and excited for what we will now achieve, together.Georgina Elizabeth Nutton NPQEL MBAExecutive Headteacher, The Barham and Preston Park Federation

pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Head of School
Welcome to Barham Primary School — a caring, inclusive school at the heart of its community, where every child matters. Barham is a warm and purposeful place built on kindness, trust and high expectations. Families quickly feel the strong sense of belonging that defines our school, and children are known, valued and supported to flourish.Having served as a senior leader at Barham for over ten years, I feel deeply connected to our community and the journey we have shared. During this time, I have worked alongside staff and families to strengthen teaching, nurture talent and continually raise aspirations for our children. It is a privilege to now serve as Interim Head of School and to continue building on the strong foundations that define Barham — with clarity, care and confidence in our shared direction.At the heart of our work is a belief in learning that makes a lasting difference. We want children to enjoy coming to school, to feel curious and confident as learners, and to leave each day proud of their achievements and inspired by what lies ahead. Learning at Barham builds secure foundations, deepens understanding over time and nurtures the resilience, confidence and character children need to thrive — both now and in the future.Our curriculum is ambitious, carefully sequenced and rooted in strong subject knowledge, with reading, language and communication at its core. We prioritise early language development, phonics and reading fluency because secure reading opens doors to the wider curriculum and enables children to achieve well across all subjects.Our impact is visible in classrooms and recognised externally. In our most recent Ofsted inspection, pupils were described as “safe, happy and kind,” and inspectors confirmed that the school “has taken effective action to maintain the standards identified at the previous inspection.” Pupils were recognised as “perform[ing] excellently in national tests,” and the breadth and ambition of the curriculum — particularly its strong focus on communication and reading — were praised.This strong foundation is further affirmed through our IQM Inclusion Review, which reaffirmed Barham’s Centre of Excellence status and celebrated the strength of our partnerships with families, effective professional collaboration and the progress pupils make from their individual starting points. National recognition from the Secretary of State for Education also highlighted the excellent outcomes achieved by disadvantaged pupils, placing Barham “among the very best nationally.” Together, these acknowledgements reflect a school that combines compassion with rigour, inclusion with high expectations and stability with continued ambition.Barham is a school where belonging drives success. We are proud of our diverse community and the inclusive culture we have built — one where children feel safe, respected and encouraged to aim high. Clear routines, consistent expectations and thoughtful pastoral care create calm, purposeful classrooms where children are ready to learn and grow.In my role, I work closely with the Executive Headteacher, governors, staff, families and federation colleagues to lead the day-to-day life of the school with integrity and steadiness. My focus remains on strengthening consistency across classrooms, investing in staff development and ensuring that high standards are sustained for every child. I believe deeply in building strong teams and fostering a professional culture rooted in collaboration, reflection and continuous improvement.Strong partnerships with families remain central to our success. We value open, honest communication and believe children thrive when school and home work together with trust and shared purpose. Our staff are dedicated, skilled and deeply committed to creating an environment where children — and adults — feel supported, valued and inspired to achieve their very best.We are proud to be part of The Barham and Preston Park Federation, united by a shared moral purpose: learning that makes a meaningful difference for every child. Federation strengthens our leadership capacity, sharpens our practice and widens opportunities for pupils, while preserving the heart and identity that make Barham special.Thank you for being part of our Barham community. We are proud of what we have achieved together and optimistic about the future — continuing to build a school where children feel they belong, achieve highly and step confidently into the next stage of their journey.Jayshree ThakoreHead of SchoolBarham Primary School

pageCache.pageTitle: Barham Primary School - Welcome to Barham
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Barham
Barham Primary School is situated in a residential area near to Wembley High Road and Ealing Road. We are a large four-form entry school admitting children from the age of 3 to 11 years. The original building dates from the 1930s. In 1991 the building was doubled in size by the completion of a new wing.
In April 2003 a new sports hall and music suite were completed. This has made the school a very spacious, bright and welcoming place.
Classes are no larger than 30 and we have additional rooms for ICT, small group music tuition, a library and nursery. We have extensive playgrounds, a large field and a nature area.
Our Children
Our children, mainly from the immediate local area, come from a variety of backgrounds, faiths and races. We are a multi-cultural school and proud to be so. We actively encourage a working partnership between parents and school in the belief that this leads to higher standards and the general well being of all children in the school.
Our Governing Body
The Governing Body is responsible for many important decisions in the running of the school, catering to the needs of the whole school community, and all its stakeholders. Governors support the school to ensure that all its statutory duties are met and the school provides the best environment for learning.
These duties include:
A current list of Governors is available on request from the school office and can be viewed on our website. You can contact the Governing Body by writing to the chair of Governors via the school office. Governors also welcome thoughts, ideas and issues that parents would like to discuss with them.
